//: Programme three's landed parcels, kept for the record and not for running. First five: unipile-core, unipile-messaging, booking-server, booking-dialog, adgrant-front. Then room-identity, login-create-room, chatwoot-inbox, booking-picker, adgrant-content, dev-agents-kb, adgrant-generate and dev-agents. What is still running is in parcels.json, and it reuses ownership these released: booking-gate inherits the booking server and the dialog, and booking-linkedin inherits the identity layer.

unipile-core.why: Four parcels in this programme call Unipile, and there is no Unipile code in the repository at all - a grep for it returns nothing. Whoever writes the second client writes a second error mapper, a second retry policy and a second opinion about where the key may live, and the third and fourth do it again. One client, first, alone, is the cheapest hour in the programme. It has no seams and no route: it is a module four other parcels import.
unipile-core.done: One HTTP client for the whole Unipile surface, server-side only. Base URL is https://${UNIPILE_DSN}/api/v1/... - the DSN carries host AND a non-standard port and differs per tenant, so api1 and 13111 appear nowhere in the code. Auth is the single header X-API-KEY, no Bearer prefix. The key authorises the ENTIRE Unipile workspace, not one account, so this directory must be unimportable from client code: read process.env at call time the way server/db.ts does, and add a test that fails if anything under client/ imports it. Errors: the RFC 7807 envelope in the brief section 1.2, mapped to a typed union keyed on `type`, with the enum values the brief lists. Retry 503 and 504 with backoff and NOTHING else; a 401 is an operator alert, never a retry - there is no Retry-After header and no documented quota anywhere, so the retry policy is ours and must be conservative. Missing env vars are not a crash and not a dead button: export an available() and an unavailableLine() the way server/waha.ts:89-115 does, so a caller can put one sentence on screen. Never log the key, never log a whole request body, and never let a Unipile error string reach a visitor unfiltered - its `detail` can name our account. accounts.ts wraps GET /api/v1/accounts and GET /api/v1/accounts/{id} so the operator page can be told whether the two accounts in the brief section 4 are connected and what their sources[].status says (OK, STOPPED, ERROR, CREDENTIALS, PERMISSIONS, CONNECTING - a connected account can rot, and this is how we learn it did). Add both UNIPILE_ variables plus UNIPILE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, UNIPILE_CALENDAR_ACCOUNT_ID and UNIPILE_WHATSAPP_ACCOUNT_ID to .env.example, each with one comment line saying what breaks without it. Tests inject fetch, as server/bridge/chatwoot.ts:57 does - no network in the suite. Do NOT build calendar, messaging or webhook calls here: three other parcels own those and each will import this one.

server/routes.ts: one call that ensures the webhook exists

unipile-messaging.why: The owner asked for two things by name: create the webhook programmatically rather than by hand in a dashboard, and always check who a message is from, who it is to, and which chat it is in. Both are this parcel. It is also the transport two later parcels stand on - the booking confirmation and the room's WhatsApp route both send and receive through it - so it is built before either and knows about neither.
unipile-messaging.done: Send, receive, and the webhook's own lifecycle. SENDING: both send routes are multipart/form-data, NOT JSON, and that is the biggest single difference from WAHA - the brief section 1.5 has the field lists. POST /api/v1/chats is documented as creating a chat if needed or using an existing one, so it is the single upsert send path; pass account_id on it as a safety rail. THE WEBHOOK, IN CODE: at route registration, GET /api/v1/webhooks, find ours by request_url, create it only when absent - idempotent, never a second one - and delete ones pointing at hosts we have retired. The address is ours to compute, ${PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/api/unipile/inbound, which is why the owner sets no URL anywhere; UNIPILE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is a random string, not an address. REGISTER TWO, and there is no third: Unipile has five webhook types and a calendar is not among them, so the calendar is polled and never pushed. One is source: messaging. The other is the account-lifecycle one, because a linked WhatsApp device can be logged out from the phone, and the difference between learning that from a webhook and discovering it from a silent send failure is a day of a room looking broken. The exact source value for account status is NOT in the webhooks page - read https://developer.unipile.com/docs/account-lifecycle and use the value that page gives. Do not guess it: a webhook registered with an invalid source is one that silently never fires, and you would report success. Both webhooks point at our one endpoint and carry the same secret, and the handler branches on the payload - an account-status event is not a message and must not reach the message path. Two documented gotchas that both fail SILENTLY and must both be handled: a webhook created by API carries no Content-Type header by default, so pass headers: [{key: Content-Type, value: application/json}] or express.json() leaves req.body empty; and there is no HMAC signature anywhere in Unipile, only a shared secret in a header you name, so use UNIPILE_WEBHOOK_SECRET compared with timingSafeEqual. server/identity.ts:466-474 shows the shape and ALSO shows the bug - when its env var is unset the check passes. Here, no secret configured means the endpoint refuses everything. Do not copy that line. THE INBOUND RULE, which is this parcel's real subject: the brief's seven checks, each its own named exported function with its own test. (1) the secret matches. (2) account_id is on an allowlist of accounts we operate, not merely present. (3) sender.attendee_provider_id !== account_info.user_id - our own sent messages arrive as message_received too and there is NO fromMe flag, so without this the room echoes our own agents back as if the visitor said it. (4) chat_id is present and is the chat expected for whatever this answers. (5) message_id has not been seen - five retries are guaranteed on any non-200 within 30s, so idempotency is not optional. (6) event === message_received; the other five events are not messages. (7) timestamp is recent, because a reconnect delivers a burst from the disconnected period. Anything failing a check is recorded and dropped, never guessed at. The body field is `message`, a string - the REST API calls it `text`, and that mismatch is a bug waiting. Reply 200 in well under 30s and do the work after. IDENTITY: attendee_provider_id is a TAGGED UNION, either <phone>@s.whatsapp.net or <id>@lid, and the second form carries no number. Model it as a union and never regex it for digits: WhatsApp's LID migration is real, Unipile's own docs contradict themselves about which form is internal, and Unipile has no LID resolver where WAHA has one. Report that in your handoff. Contact reads are GET /api/v1/chats/{chat_id}/attendees and GET /api/v1/chat_attendees/{id}: you get name (a self-set push name, display only), picture_url and provider_id, and there is no phone field and no WhatsApp branch of specifics. This parcel does not touch server/identity.ts or server/waha.ts - room-identity owns that swap and will import you.

client/src/App.tsx: one route for the AdGrant.AI tree

adgrant-front.why: adgrant.ai today is a Vite React SPA on Google App Engine whose shell has not changed in three weeks, whose HTML is an empty root div, whose stylesheet is 104KB, whose single bundle is 652KB with no code-splitting, which requests TWENTY-EIGHT Google Fonts families at once - a theme-switcher list, not a design decision - which localises itself with a hidden Google Translate gadget setting a googtrans cookie, and which disables pinch-zoom. It also has 74 real pages of real content and a pitch worth keeping: free instant launch of traffic from your Google Ad Grant account, message us the Customer ID and go live. This parcel builds the new front of it in the design system that already exists here, from material that already exists here.
adgrant-front.done: A new AdGrant.AI front page and shell, in this application, at its own route tree - NOT on a second host, and the reason is in the frozen list: client/index.html carries the one head this application serves, so a second site with its own title and meta cannot be done without editing a frozen file. That switch is owner work for when no wave is running. So build it so it CAN move: no import of the top-rated.team header or footer, its own chrome, and nothing that assumes the apex. WRITE IT FROM WHAT IS HERE, not from invention. client/src/components/site/doors/adgrant-style.ts already establishes this product's identity inside our system - one remapped accent, the wordmark, and a note that a second font or a second colour anywhere else would undo the system it sits in. Extend that deliberately rather than starting a new palette. ADGRANT_LIBRARY at :17-27 already names the five sections of the live site with a line each and links them without copying them: keep that discipline. THE 74 LIBRARY PAGES STAY WHERE THEY ARE and are linked. Moving them is a separate programme, and breaking 74 indexed URLs in order to redesign a front page would be the most expensive kind of tidy. data/kb/kb.adgrant-ai.json is our own written material on this product and data/kb/kb.ad-grants.json is Google's own documentation of the programme; both are already built, and the eligibility and policy facts in the second are the ones this page must not get wrong - a nonprofit reading a wrong eligibility line loses a grant worth 10k a month. client/src/components/workspace/AdGrantPanel.tsx and AD_GRANT_SETUP are the setup this product actually performs, in order; describe that rather than a feature list. FIX WHAT THE LIVE SITE GETS WRONG rather than reproducing it: real type in two faces, not twenty-eight; no pinch-zoom lock; and no machine-translation gadget standing in for localisation - English only is an honest state and a googtrans cookie is not. The page ends in a room: the ad-grants door already exists with its own agent and corpus, so the action is to open a room on this product, not a contact form. Set the page's own title and description the way client/src/pages/landing.tsx does, in the page, since the shell's are not yours to edit. data/build-shots/adgrant-ai.png is a screenshot of the OLD site, shown on a builds card here - say in your handoff that it needs replacing, and do not replace it yourself.

shared/api.ts: the booking request and response types

booking-server.why: Booking is Google's own overlay today: a third-party script, a 1x1 clipped host div, and a hidden button we click. It works, and it means the visitor leaves our page into Google's UI, we learn nothing about the booking, and the availability logic is Google's. This is the server half of replacing it. It exists before the popup so the popup has something true to talk to, and both build to the shapes the brief fixes in writing.
booking-server.done: GET /api/booking/slots, POST /api/booking and GET /api/booking/confirmed, exactly as the brief section 3 specifies them - those shapes are a contract with a parcel running in the same wave and may not drift. THERE IS NO FREE/BUSY ENDPOINT IN UNIPILE: seven calendar routes exist and none of them is availability, so we compute it. Read the primary calendar ONCE (GET /api/v1/calendars, take is_primary, assert is_read_only === false, keep its id and its own timezone) and cache it - not per widget load. Then list events over a window PADDED BY A DAY ON EACH SIDE with expand_recurring=true, and do the overlap test yourself. Three traps, each of which silently shows a busy day as free, and each needs a test with a fixture that fails without it. (1) An all-day event is {date} with NO date_time, so new Date(ev.start.date_time) is Invalid Date on the owner's holiday and the week reads as open - branch on "date" in ev.start and treat it as busy for the whole date in the calendar's zone. (2) start and end are CONTAINMENT filters: the docs say starting-after and ending-before, so a 09:00-10:00 event is excluded from a 09:30-11:00 query while still blocking it. That is why the window is padded and the real test is ours. (3) Without expand_recurring a weekly standup arrives as one master event with an RRULE array and is invisible to the calculation. Do not trust the undocumented busy=true alone: filter on is_cancelled !== true AND transparency !== transparent AND an event_type not in a declined/birthday set, so the rule is readable and testable rather than a server-side interpretation nobody documented. Cache the computed window server-side for 30-60s; never one Unipile call per rendered calendar cell. WRITING THE BOOKING: POST the event with transparency: opaque, conference: {provider: google_meet} and no url (which auto-provisions the Meet link), and notify: true - notify DEFAULTS TO FALSE, and without it the visitor never gets an invite, which is the whole reason we are not connecting their calendar. The 201 returns only {event_id}, not the event, so GET it back if you want the Meet URL. TWO THINGS THE DOCS DO NOT SETTLE, and you must settle them by experiment rather than by guess, then write what you found into your handoff: whether attendees: [] satisfies the required constraint (schema-valid, untested - fall back to the visitor's own address, which we collect, or to dan@top-rated.team), and whether date_time must be UTC-with-Z while time_zone is advisory (the docs say ISO 8601 UTC datetime AND carry a separate time_zone field, which is contradictory). Send both, then read the created event out of Google Calendar and confirm the real hour before you report done - a booking widget that is an hour out is worse than none. code.ts mints the planted WhatsApp code: the alphabet at server/identity.ts:98-102, with no dash, underscore, I, O, 0 or 1, because it gets dictated - a nanoid with dashes once broke about 40% of binds and the comment there records it. Export the regex so the handler and the test share one pattern. Five-minute expiry, and /confirmed reads it back. Register a matcher with server/unipile/inbound.ts rather than parsing a webhook yourself: the seven checks belong to one parcel. email is the ONLY optional field; without it the event is still created and invited is false, and a placeholder address built from a phone number is permitted only where there IS a number and must never be reported to the visitor as an invite that will arrive. Do NOT build visitor-calendar connection: the brief section 2.3 prices it and refuses it.

booking-dialog.why: The owner asked for our own booking popup in our own style. The trap is the call sites: there are SEVENTEEN book-a-call anchors in eleven files, plus a slash command in the room, plus a hardcoded link in the frozen index.html. A parcel that edits seventeen call sites collides with every other parcel in its wave and several in the next. So this one changes what the hook DOES and not what it RETURNS, and touches no call site at all.
booking-dialog.done: Our popup, opened by the same useBooking() the site already spreads. THE CONTRACT THAT MAY NOT CHANGE: useBooking() returns exactly { onClick, onMouseEnter, onFocus } (client/src/hooks/use-booking.ts:75), spread as {...booking} at seventeen sites. Keep all three keys and their meanings. Warming stays: a module-level one-shot listener on the first pointerdown, touchstart, keydown or scroll anywhere on the page, because there is no hover on a phone and touchstart is only about 50ms ahead of click - the reasoning at :16-27 still holds, only now it warms a slots fetch instead of Google's script. The modifier-key and middle-click bail-outs at :53-62 stay exactly as they are: a cmd-click must still open a tab. WHAT INVERTS: today the href is a real fallback because a third-party script can be blocked, so preventDefault is conditional. Now the popup is ours, so preventDefault becomes unconditional on a plain left click - but the href STAYS as the no-JS path, and target=_blank comes off nothing. Delete bookingReady(), which is exported with no caller anywhere in the tree. THE POPUP: lazily imported with the exact incantation the five LeadDialog hosts use (client/src/components/site/Header.tsx:10 and four others). The reason is stated there - LeadDialog pulls in Radix and the header is in the landing chunk paid traffic downloads first - and a second eager Radix dialog regresses it. Match LeadDialog's Radix usage, its focus and Escape handling, its light and dark treatment, and the site's own type and colour tokens. There is no ui/dialog wrapper in use: grep proves it has no importer, so import Radix directly as LeadDialog does. Read GET /api/booking/slots and POST /api/booking exactly as the brief section 3 fixes them; that is a contract with a parcel in your own wave. Slots arrive as local wall-clock times in a named timezone, which is what a human picks - print the timezone beside them, because a visitor in another country booking a 14:00 needs to know whose 14:00 it is. A day with no slots is present and empty: say nothing is free rather than hiding the day. ONE optional field, email, with a sentence saying what it buys (a real calendar invite) and what its absence costs (nothing else). A 409 is not an error to swallow: the response carries fresh availability, so redraw with it and say the time was just taken. On a phone, the save button opens the WhatsApp deep link from the response and then polls GET /api/booking/confirmed, so the confirmation lands in the popup the visitor came from as well as in WhatsApp; on a desktop the same button just confirms. THE ROOM'S SLASH COMMAND: client/src/components/workspace/Composer.tsx:220-228 bypasses the hook because a slash command has no click to fall through, and its comment says so. Give it an imperative open that resolves without an event, and leave its window.open fallback working. THE ASKWIDGET COMPOSITION MUST SURVIVE: three anchors at AskWidget.tsx:449, :477 and :539 spread {...booking} BEFORE a local onClick that calls onAskedForAPerson?.() and then booking.onClick(event). Both orders are load-bearing and both are recorded there as bugs that already happened: the JSX order because spreading after replaces the handler and loses the signal, the runtime order because booking.onClick may navigate and a signal recorded after navigation is never recorded. You are changing what booking.onClick does, so read those three sites and verify the signal still fires first.

server/routes.ts: one route for the claim state

room-identity.why: Three of the owner's asks are one feature: let a room's owner name it, let a room be claimed so it is theirs, and make that survive a deploy. Today a room's name is written once at the instant of creation and is immutable through every interface this product has - four independent checks confirm it, including a grep for renameWorkspace that returns nothing - and the identity bindings that would say who owns a room live in a new Map() that empties on restart. Alone in its wave because it writes into the room, the storage layer and the identity layer, and everything reads those.
room-identity.done: A room that can be named by whoever owns it, and an ownership that survives a deploy. THE TABLE: a new table in shared/schema-rooms.ts, re-exported from shared/schema.ts in ONE line - drizzle-kit follows the export, and fifteen lines in a seam do not merge. It holds what server/identity.ts:109-116 already models - workspaceId, provider, providerId, displayName, boundAt - and the first binding on a room is its owner. Persist through server/identity-store.ts, so server/identity.ts stops being the store as well as the logic, and keep the in-memory path as the fallback when there is no database. THERE IS NO DATABASE ON THE DEPLOYMENT TODAY: DATABASE_URL is unset, rooms live in memory, and every deploy destroys them. A claim written to a table that does not exist is the bug the owner already reported. Say so in your handoff, plainly, as the thing that blocks this feature from meaning anything - do not quietly ship it and call it done. THE NAME: add a rename to the Storage interface (server/storage.ts:82-93 - nine writes and a touch, none of which updates a workspace), implemented in BOTH MemoryStorage and PgStorage and wired through the delegating object; an updateWorkspaceSchema beside the createWorkspaceSchema that already caps a name at 120; a PATCH route; and a ServerEvent so other people in the room see the new name without reloading - server/ws.ts is how state reaches them. Only the owner may rename. An unclaimed room has no owner, so the control appears once a claim exists, and a room nobody has claimed keeps the name roomName() gave it. THE CONTROL, and the standing instruction is DO NOT COMPLICATE THE ROOM: the name is already on screen in three places (WorkspaceSidebar.tsx:153-155, the desktop top bar at workspace.tsx:187-191, and the owner's lead notifications), and the smallest honest affordance is to make the one the owner already reads editable in place. No new panel, no settings screen, no modal for one text field. IDENTITY, AND THIS DECISION IS ALREADY MADE: LinkedIn stays on the official Sign In with LinkedIn (OIDC), which is built, tested and correct. The brief section 2.1 prices the alternative and refuses it; the short version is that Unipile hosted auth would bill EUR 5 per claimed room per month - more than the entire AI budget of the room it identifies - and would ask the visitor for their LinkedIn PASSWORD on a third-party page that may present a captcha. Do not switch it. Leave the scope at openid profile: adding email is a review cost, not a free upgrade. WHATSAPP: swap the transport from WAHA to server/unipile/messaging.ts, for OUR OWN NUMBER ONLY. WAHA does exactly two jobs - probeWaha() at server/waha.ts:89-115 learns our own number so the wa.me link has a destination, and an inbound webhook delivers the reply - and Unipile does both for one account at no per-visitor cost. What the VISITOR does must not change: they tap a wa.me link and message us. That direction is also the safe one - Unipile's own provider limits say a fresh account can be blocked after two or three new outbound chats, while replying to inbound is effectively unlimited. Keep the sha256(pepper, chatId) identifier at :387-389: a phone number is never stored and never logged. Keep the dictatable nonce alphabet and BIND_CODE_RE. Keep binding as an allowance rather than a gate - allowanceForWorkspace() at :164-179 gives a bound room three times the turns and budget, and the room address stays a bearer credential. AND KEEP THE THIRD ROUTE the owner asked for: we do not know a person's WhatsApp, so adding a number to a room by hand must remain possible and must not be dressed up as verification. A number somebody typed is a note; a number that messaged us is a proof; the room must not print them the same way. RoomIdentityDialog is the popup a newly created room shows to offer the claim - login-create-room opens it from the site in the next wave, and you do not need to know how.

login-create-room.why: The owner wants the Open-a-room links on the site to become one control doing both halves of the same job: get back into a room you already have, or start a new one and be offered ownership of it. The list of rooms this browser remembers already exists and is already maintained - twelve of them, newest first, in localStorage - and /w with no token already renders it. What is missing is that the list is reachable only from an address nobody types.
login-create-room.done: One control where Open a room is now, reading a list that already exists. THE LIST IS NOT NEW: listStoredWorkspaces() in client/src/hooks/use-workspace.ts:48-58 returns the remembered rooms newest first and returns [] rather than throwing in private mode; rememberWorkspace() keeps the last twelve; client/src/App.tsx:51 already routes /w with no token to them. Present that list; do not build a second store. And do not import the room's chunk to do it - the site's landing chunk is what paid traffic downloads and the workspace bundle is 198KB of it. Either export the reader from somewhere the site can import without pulling the room in, or read localStorage directly behind the same try/catch guard. THE CONTROL: two actions fused into one, as the owner described - the left half returns you to a room, the right half makes one. Hover opens the list on a pointer device; on a phone there is no hover, so the return half opens it on tap and the create half creates. A browser that remembers no room must not show an empty menu: with nothing to return to, the control is only the create action, and it says so. Every entry needs its name, and this is where the owner's other complaint lands - he saw three rooms all called Conversion tracking, because the name was a hardcoded fallback. server/storage.ts:264-272 fixed the fallback and room-identity makes the name editable; the menu shows whatever a room is called plus when it was last seen, so two rooms from the same door are still tellable apart. CREATE: use-open-room.ts already stamps the general-room source and navigates to /w/:token; after it lands, the room offers the claim through the dialog room-identity built in the previous wave. Do not build a second claim UI, and do not put the claim in the site's chunk. THE CALL SITES YOU OWN, and they are why this parcel is late in the programme: Header.tsx (desktop nav and the phone burger), FirstScreen.tsx (the hero, where OPEN A ROOM currently comes first, before BOOK A CALL), doors.tsx and door.tsx (each door's hero and its panel band). Keep the order the owner established - the room action first, then Book a call, then Leave a message - and keep the capitalisation he asked for. On a door, the room opened must still be that door's room and not the general one: the source stamp is what decides that, and it is easy to lose while moving a button. Nothing here may change what a booking anchor does. booking-dialog owns the hook, and you own some of the files its anchors sit in, so leave every {...booking} spread and every href exactly as you found it - including the three composed onClick handlers around AskWidget.

chatwoot-inbox.why: The owner wants contractors to answer a room from ChatWoot. Most of that is built and none of it is reachable: 139 lines of client, 756 of orchestration, 210 of attribution and 466 of tests exist, and BridgePanel is imported nowhere - data/builds/top-rated-team.json:30 records that as deliberate, so nothing on the site claims a bridge the room does not offer. What is actually missing is two things: the panel is not mounted, and the design asks the owner to paste one conversation id per room, which does not scale past him doing it by hand.
chatwoot-inbox.done: A room that can talk to ChatWoot without anybody pasting an id, and a panel a person can reach. FIRST, THE CONSTITUTION: docs/parcels-programme-1.json:329-350 is the parcel that specified this bridge, and its done text still binds. Attribution is the whole job and the rest is plumbing. Every outbound message names its speaker from the room's member record, not from whoever typed. An agent's message must never arrive looking like a person's. An unmappable inbound sender is marked unattributed, never guessed. A bridged agent turn claims through server/spend.ts, because there is prior art of an unguarded endpoint being hit for five hours. THE ROOM TOKEN NEVER APPEARS IN AN OUTBOUND PAYLOAD. A delivery failure surfaces on the message, not in a log. Contradict none of it. THE CHANGE: today server/bridge/chatwoot.ts:55-91 speaks the application API - POST /api/v1/accounts/{accountId}/conversations/{conversationId}/messages with an api_access_token - which is right for speaking as an agent into one conversation the owner found by hand, and wrong for a room that should make its own. Add the API-Inbox client path, so a room creates its own contact and its own conversation in an inbox keyed by inbox_identifier and contact_identifier, and keep the agent path for what it is good at. Correlate a conversation to a room the way index.ts:91 already does, by an accountId-and-conversationId key, and carry the room's identity in ChatWoot custom attributes rather than in message text - the token must not travel. FOUR EXISTING WEAKNESSES TO FIX WHILE YOU ARE IN HERE, each verified in the code. (1) Echo suppression at chatwoot.ts:128 tests only for agent_bot and private, not for message_type === outgoing, which is exactly what our own API-sent message comes back as, so our messages can loop. (2) The dedupe key at index.ts:260-269 is the first 80 characters of the body with a 30-minute TTL, so two genuine thanks half an hour apart collapse into one. (3) Webhook auth at index.ts:240-252 RETURNS TRUE WHEN NO ENV VAR IS SET - an open webhook by default, which must become a refusal. (4) The whole bridge map is in process memory by design (index.ts:10-12, a restart forgets every bridge), which is honest but must be said on screen where a person connects one. MOUNT THE PANEL, and the standing instruction is not to complicate the room: it is plumbing, it belongs where a room's other plumbing lives, and it must be invisible to a visitor who has no bridge. A panel that is empty for everyone except the owner does not belong on the first screen.

booking-picker.why: The booking popup works and the owner does not like how it asks for a date. It is a vertical list of days, each with its own row of times folded underneath, so choosing a Thursday afternoon means scrolling past Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday. He wants it horizontal: pick the day of a month in one place, pick the time beside it or under it. This parcel changes only that, and only in the one file.
booking-picker.done: A two-pane picker. On a wide screen: a month grid of days on the left, and the times for the selected day on the right. On a phone the same two panes stack, grid above times, because a 7-column grid and a column of times side by side at 375px is neither. Nothing else about the popup changes - not the email field, not the WhatsApp deep link, not the polling, not the 409 redraw, not the expired-code retry. FOUR THINGS THAT ARE ALREADY RIGHT AND MUST SURVIVE. (1) A day with nothing free is PRESENT with an empty array, at four layers, and each layer is pinned: server/booking/slots.ts:261 pushes the day outside the weekend guard and says why at :11-12; server/booking/slots.test.ts:238-264 asserts fourteen days come back and that a Saturday's slots deep-equal []; client/src/lib/booking.ts:169-185 copies it through, pinned at client/src/lib/booking.test.ts:114-120; and the dialog prints a sentence. Keep the sentence. A grid that silently omits a day is a worse answer than one that says nothing is free. (2) The timezone is stated beside the times, because a visitor in another country booking a 14:00 needs to know whose 14:00 it is. (3) firstDayWithASlot falls back to days[0] when EVERY day is empty, which leaves a date selected, no time, and the submit disabled - correct but silent. Say something in that case: nothing free in this window. (4) The 409 response carries fresh availability and redraws. A GRID HAS CONVENTIONS AND THIS ONE MUST FOLLOW THEM: arrow keys move by day and wrap across rows, PageUp and PageDown move by month, Home and End go to the start and end of a row, one tab stop for the whole grid with a roving tabindex, and the selected day announced in a live region along with how many times are free in it. Give the grid role=grid and the day cells role=gridcell, and mark a day with no free time aria-disabled rather than only grey. DO NOT LET IT GO BACKWARDS PAST TODAY: server/booking/slots.ts:70-75 validates a date's shape and realness and does NOT reject a past one, so a previous-month request is answered 200 with every day empty, which reads as a broken picker. Disable back-navigation client-side. And DERIVE THE GRID FROM THE RESPONSE, not the browser clock - from days[0].date and the response's own timezone - or a visitor in another zone sees a day greyed for no visible reason.

adgrant-content.why: adgrant.ai holds 23 written pages and 12 starter templates behind an unauthenticated JSON API, and a rebuilt site needs that material in this repository rather than fetched from Google App Engine at runtime. It also needs it CORRECTED: the pages are one machine-generated batch and six statements in them are wrong against Google's current documentation. Carrying them into a better typeface without fixing them would mean more people believing them.
adgrant-content.done: A build script and a generated module, in the shape scripts/build-blog.ts and scripts/build-cases.ts already use - read both before writing a line, and match them: a script reads sources into data/, writes shared/<thing>.ts, and the generated file carries the do-not-edit banner. THE FETCH. GET https://adgrant.ai/api/content/pages?category={glossary|case-studies|tricks}&pageSize=100 for the index, then GET https://adgrant.ai/api/content/page/{category}/{slug} for each body, and GET https://adgrant.ai/api/templates plus /api/templates/stats. No auth. Keep per page: slug, category, title, topic, niche, excerpt, bodyMarkdown, metaTitle, metaDescription, keywords, heroImage, heroImageAlt, relatedLinks, publishedAt. Write each page to data/adgrant/<category>/<slug>.md with that as frontmatter and the markdown as the body, so a correction is a diff a person can read and review. The script is re-runnable and must not clobber a local correction silently: if a fetched body differs from the one on disk, say so and leave the disk copy, unless run with a flag that says to take theirs. THE SIX CORRECTIONS, each verified against Google's live pages and each listed in the brief section 1 with the URL - apply every one, in the markdown, with a note in the frontmatter saying what was corrected and against which page. (1) The 5% CTR rule deactivates after TWO CONSECUTIVE months, not one. (2) $10,000 / $2 / 30 days is 166.7 clicks a day, not 329 - 329 is the dollar budget - and the dependent impressions figure is wrong with it; two pages in this corpus currently contradict each other by a factor of two. (3) The two-ads-per-ad-group rule stopped applying to grantees on 30 June 2022; two ad GROUPS per campaign is what is still required. (4) The remarketing list minimum was never 500. (5) Ad Rank has no published formula and Google does not name Quality Score in it. (6) The Ad Grant website policies link is dead; the live page is support.google.com/nonprofits/answer/1657899. ALSO: the whole bypass-the-$2-cap framing assumes manual CPC is the default, and it has not been for accounts created since 22 April 2019 - rewrite the framing, do not delete the fact. AND STRIP EVERY UNSOURCED PERCENTAGE: 600+ accounts I've managed, 30-50% of incremental clicks, 15-25% higher CTR, 15-40% conversion lift, and any sibling. They repeat verbatim across all fifteen generated pages and none is sourced. There is a real number to use instead and the script must expose it: /api/templates/stats returns 4,539 accounts processed, 16,575 campaigns, 3,142,469 keywords, with medians. Put the stats in the generated module as data. Do not invent a replacement figure for anything you delete - a sentence with no number is fine. Tests: the generated module parses, every page has a slug and a body, no page contains any of the stripped phrases, and the six corrections are each asserted by a test that fails if the wrong wording comes back on a refetch.

one appended Corpus const for Unipile
both names on the CORPORA line

dev-agents-kb.why: Two agents in the next wave answer about the Google Ads API and about Unipile, and an agent with useKb set and nothing to read retrieves nothing at all - silently. shared/roster.ts says it outright: an agent answering out of the wrong documentation would be worse than one that admits it has nothing. So the corpora exist first, in their own wave, and the agents that read them come after.
dev-agents-kb.done: Two corpora, built the way every other corpus in data/kb is built. Read scripts/build-kb.ts end to end first: how a Corpus is declared, what the fetch and chunking do, what the guards check. THE SEAM IS WIDENED FOR THIS PARCEL AND ONLY THIS ONE. The stated exception admits one appended Corpus const; this parcel appends two, plus both names on the CORPORA line. That is the same merge shape - a contiguous append at the end of a list - and no other parcel in this wave touches that file. Do not take it as licence to restructure anything in it. NAMESPACES: google-ads-api and unipile-api. Note they are deliberately NOT google-ads and not the existing ad-grants: those are corpora about running campaigns, and an agent asked how to authenticate against the API must not answer out of a page about bidding. SOURCES. For Google Ads: developers.google.com/google-ads/api - the access levels and developer token pages, OAuth2 and the login-customer-id header, the mutate services for campaign budget, campaign, ad group, keyword, responsive search ad and sitelink, temporary resource ids, batching, and the quota page. For Unipile: developer.unipile.com - and note it serves a markdown twin at <url>.md with an index at /llms.txt, which is the reliable way to read it because the rendered pages are JavaScript. Cover accounts and hosted auth, chats and messages, calendars and events, and webhooks. Every chunk must carry its source URL, because an agent that cites a page a reader can open is the whole point and there is a test in this repository that enforces it per corpus. Run the existing corpus guards and satisfy them: no chunk shorter than the minimum letter count, no chunk from one corpus carrying another's host, entities decoded. Report the chunk count per namespace in your handoff, and report honestly if a section could not be fetched rather than shipping a corpus with a hole in it.

server/routes.ts: one POST route that generates a structure
one GET route for the remaining generations
shared/api.ts: the generation request and response types

adgrant-generate.why: The owner wants the AdGrant.AI home page to stop being a form and start being an agent that asks what is needed and then generates. That sentence contains two products with a Google-shaped approval in the middle, and the brief section 2 separates them. This parcel builds the half that needs no approval from anybody: generate a complete, policy-checked account structure and show it. Writing it into a live grant account needs a developer token at Basic Access, an OAuth client, and a manager link a human at the nonprofit has to accept in the Google Ads UI - which no page can promise inside one session.
adgrant-generate.done: Generate an Ad Grant account structure from a nonprofit's website, check it against Google's rules, and count it. THE POLICY GATE IS THE MOST VALUABLE PART OF THIS PARCEL, so build it first and test it hardest: pure functions over the generated object, no network, every input listed in the brief section 2. It must reject a structure that has a single-word keyword outside Google's exception list, fewer than two ad groups in a campaign, fewer than two sitelinks, no geo-target, a destination that is not https on an authorised domain, a daily budget over $329, or manual CPC where Smart bidding is required. A generator that produces a structure Google would suspend is worse than no generator, and the nonprofit carries that risk, not us. Each rule is its own named exported function with its own test and its own citation in a comment. THE QUOTA: three generations, durable, per identified person - and durable means a table, so shared/schema-adgrant.ts holds it and shared/schema.ts re-exports it in ONE line, because a table is fifteen lines and the seam allows three. Count a generation when the structure is produced, not when it is requested. Say the remaining count on every response; a limit a visitor discovers by hitting it is a bad limit. AND SAY WHY THREE, because it is not arbitrary: the Google Ads API allows 15,000 operations a day across every client of a developer token, and a generation is roughly 150 of them. IDENTITY: a generation requires a bound room, through the identity layer that already exists - LinkedIn OIDC or the WhatsApp click-to-chat proof, both in server/identity.ts. Do not build a third way in. Read the brief's other file, docs/specs/unipile-rooms-and-booking.md section 0.1, before touching identity. WHAT YOU MUST NOT BUILD: no Google Ads API client, no OAuth, no customer id, no upload. There is no google-ads dependency in this repository and this parcel does not add one. The structure is produced, shown, and exportable as CSV for Google Ads Editor, which is a real thing a nonprofit can use today without giving us access to anything. If a sentence anywhere in your work implies the structure was uploaded, change the sentence.

shared/roster.ts: one appended agent entry for Google Ads Dev
one appended agent entry for LinkedIn Dev

dev-agents.why: The owner wants two agents that help a client build their own agents against Google Ads and against LinkedIn, present in every Google Ads, paid ads and dev room. He also asked whether they need a higher limit to do anything good. They do, and there is no per-agent limit in this codebase at all - every bound in server/spend.ts is keyed by room - so the ceiling and the agents arrive together or the agents arrive useless.
dev-agents.done: Two agents, in the right rooms, with a ceiling of their own. THE AGENTS: google-ads-dev, grounded in the google-ads-api namespace, and linkedin-dev, grounded in unipile-api - both corpora built in the previous wave. Two appended entries at the end of AGENTS, which widens the stated one-entry exception for this parcel only; the shape is still one contiguous append and nothing else in shared/roster.ts moves. WHAT THEY ARE FOR, and write the prompts to it: design and review, not build. They read the API documentation they are grounded in and tell a client what is possible, what it costs in approvals, what the quota is, what shape the code takes, and what is wrong with the code they already have. A room with a five-dollar monthly budget cannot pay for an agent to write a production integration, and a prompt that implies otherwise sells something the budget cannot deliver. LINKEDIN DEV IS WHITE-LABEL: it never names Unipile to a visitor. We are the developer; which vendor sits underneath is ours, and the agent talks about what can be built, not about whose API does it. Google Ads Dev may name Google, because the client's own account and Google's own documentation are the subject. THE ROOMS: read how an agent reaches a room before changing anything - an agent in AGENTS is reachable in every room already, and being SEEDED into one is a different thing that costs a channel and a member row per room. Decide which of the two senses the owner's every Google Ads, paid ads and dev room means, say which you chose and why in your handoff, and if you seed, seed only the doors that qualify. THE CEILING, and this is the substantial half of the parcel. server/spend.ts today keys every bound by workspaceId; agentId reaches it twice and neither is a limit. Add a per-agent ledger keyed with the agent id alongside the room's, and claim TWICE - the agent's key first, then the room's - which is exactly what routes.ts:1048-1049 already does for the ask keys. Copy that pattern rather than inventing one. The room's own bound stays over the top, so one agent can never spend the room's whole month. The numbers live in a map in server/spend.ts and NOT on AgentDef: shared/roster.ts is imported by client code, and a per-agent dollar figure on an agent row ships a cost number to the browser. claimAgentTurn already takes budgetUsd as its third argument, so the money half is nearly free; the turns-per-hour half reads a module constant at :229 and has to be parameterised. Do not touch ROOM_MONTHLY_BUDGET_USD or the two bounds under it - render.yaml is frozen and its own comment says those are not configurable. NOT IN THIS PARCEL: bring-your-own-key. The brief section 3.3 prices it - one client from one env var, no field on AgentTurn, both secret stores in memory, and a house rule that forbids agents to accept a pasted credential. Nor a pricing row: there is already a $49/month row, an earlier one was cut for a reason that applies again, and the reseller question is the owner's to answer.
